bibliographic.title: Library Information System Audit Senayan Library Management System (SLiMS) Using ISO 9126
bibliographic.venue: Proceeding of the Second International Conference on Business and Communication (ICBC 2018)
bibliographic.citation_apa: Pamungkas, P. D. A. (2018). Library information system audit Senayan Library Management System (SLiMS) using ISO 9126. In Proceeding of the Second International Conference on Business and Communication (ICBC 2018) (pp. 255–256).

methodology.sample_description: University librarians in charge at Indonesian higher education libraries using SLiMS
methodology.technology_context: open-source library management information system (SLiMS) audited with ISO 9126 via Google Forms questionnaires

eligibility.exclusion_reason: Study audits traditional library management software (SLiMS) quality using ISO 9126 questionnaires; no LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, agents, RAG, or governance of conversational AI in regulated contexts.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper mentions education, law, standards, and information system audit, its focus is software quality assessment of a PHP/MySQL library management system. It does not address conversational AI, LLM-based systems, generative AI governance, guardrails, observability of AI outputs, human oversight of AI, or comparable governance mechanisms required by the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Topic mismatch is explicit in title, abstract, and methodology; exclusion does not depend on ambiguous keyword overlap.

appraisal.notes: Internally coherent descriptive survey for ISO 9126 software quality audit of SLiMS, but small convenience sample (n=10) and limited discussion of limitations; not appraised for inclusion in LLM conversational governance synthesis.

cerqual.explanation: Findings are coherent for library IS quality assessment but have very low relevance to conversational governance of LLM systems; small sample and narrow context further limit usefulness for the target review.

synthesis.main_claim: SLiMS meets ISO 9126 quality criteria at a VERY GOOD level for managing university libraries, based on questionnaires completed by librarians at ten Indonesian universities.
synthesis.contribution: Provides an ISO 9126-based audit framework applied to the open-source SLiMS library management system in Indonesian higher education settings.
synthesis.limitations: Small voluntary sample of ten institutions; descriptive quantitative design without broader validation; no discussion of AI, conversational interfaces, or generative system governance.
synthesis.use_in_review: exclude; peripheral at best as generic IS audit precedent, not evidence on conversational or LLM governance in regulated environments.

evidence.claim: Article concerns library IS audit of SLiMS using ISO 9126, not LLM or conversational AI.
evidence.excerpt: The implementation of the SLiMS information system audit in several university libraries refers to the ISO 9126 standard

evidence.claim: Empirical design is descriptive quantitative questionnaire survey.
evidence.excerpt: The research was conducted by using descriptive quantitative method.

evidence.claim: Sample comprises ten university librarians who completed questionnaires.
evidence.excerpt: only ten universities librarians in charge who are willing to fill out the questionnaires

evidence.claim: Technology context is traditional library management software, not generative or conversational AI.
evidence.excerpt: Senayan Library Management System (SLiMS) is a library management system software with open source licensed under GPL v3

evidence.claim: Regulated education context is background for libraries, not AI governance in regulated domains.
evidence.excerpt: the library serves to support the National Education System as regulated by Law Number 20 Year 2003 on National Education System

evidence.claim: Main finding is software quality rating VERY GOOD.
evidence.excerpt: SLiMS included in the category VERY GOOD for use in the management of libraries in college

evidence.claim: Audit definition concerns conventional information system asset and integrity evaluation.
evidence.excerpt: An information system audit is the process of collecting and evaluating facts to determine whether an information system protects assets, has data integrity

evidence.claim: No LLM, chatbot, agent, RAG, or conversational governance content appears in provided text.
evidence.excerpt: Keywords: library, Senayan Library Management System (SLiMS), audit information system, ISO 9126.
